items_missed: Never asked for or used the customer's name — not once in a 20-minute call
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight into inventory with no roadmap or time expectation
Never recapped the quote form or confirmed the move details already on file
Never confirmed origin or destination address/zip — accepted the customer's '10 miles' as the only distance data point
Never asked about stairs or floors at either home, despite the customer twice referencing a second floor with furniture on it
No special-considerations probe — long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns
No access-concerns probe — parking, gate access, HOA restrictions (customer mentioned 'get the gate ready' and it went unexplored)
No moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
No Worries Damage Coverage never explained — 'insurance' was named as included in the rate and nothing more, even after a plant liability waiver came up
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no prep-shortens-the-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, on a self-pack customer moving in 48 hours
Estimate risk: 2 movers / 1 truck / 4.5-6.5 hrs quoted for a 2,006 sqft home with 40+ boxes, second-floor couches, plants and instruments, with stairs never verified
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email
Told the customer 'you do not have to respond to that email' instead of asking them to reply with corrections
Never gave office hours or how to reach the company
No walk-distance discussion and no equivalents/school-bus style reference to make the time range concrete
top_strength: Excellent proactive FAQ handling under a heavy language barrier — he volunteered the heat/breakage risk on the plants and the liability waiver, flagged the wall-mount reinstall limitation before the customer could be surprised by it, and recommended the 8:30 AM window with a real reason (heat and afternoon traffic). His clock explanation was complete and he re-confirmed it patiently when the customer circled back on when time starts and stops.
coaching_note: Garrison quoted 2 movers and 1 truck for a 2,006 sqft home without ever asking about stairs — and the customer had already said twice that there were couches on a second floor. He also skipped the entire Save Your Ass prep speech on a customer who is self-packing with a move 48 hours away, which is the single cheapest lever he had to protect that 4.5-6.5 hour range. Next call: before you build the estimate, ask stairs/floors and walk distance at BOTH addresses, then deliver the prep speech — 'the more you consolidate before we get there, the shorter the move and the lower your bill' — with the toys/drawers/carload examples.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and consistently agreeable through a difficult language barrier, but warmth came out as repeated 'perfect, perfect' filler rather than real rapport — zero name use, no humor, and no acknowledgment of the stress of a move happening in two days.
audio_review_reason: Customer side of the transcript is heavily garbled throughout, making it hard to judge how much of the repeated re-confirmation was Garrison building rapport versus the two of them talking past each other; audio would settle the phone-presence read.
